crm_notes: Key ask: deterministic latency for personalization storefront calls (95th pctl < 120ms) under steady traffic of 1200 qps peak.
Throughput target: support 1200 qps overall with spikes to 2500 qps during sales events; want guaranteed reserved capacity and burst policy.
Traffic shaping requirements: per-route priority lanes (high/normal/low), per-tenant isolation, route-level quotas, token-based metering.
Noisy-neighbor controls: automatic throttling and eviction policies, real-time telemetry to surface hot tenants, and explicit remediation SLA (detection time < 5 min, mitigation within 15 min).
Model preferences: prefer Llama-3 / MPT-class open variants; open to quantized 4-bit for cost reduction but need quality regressions testing.
Fallback plan: automatic downgrade to smaller model or routed to lower-cost Dedicated pool when latency SLO is in danger; want canary + fallback policies exposed in console.
SLA asks: uptime 99.95% for Dedicated pool, latency SLOs per-route, credits for missed SLOs, predictable monthly committed spend with true-up options.
Observability: token-level and route-level latency histograms, KV-cache hit rates, per-GPU utilization, and exported traces to their Datadog account.
POC success criteria: meet 95p < 120ms at target qps for 72h soak at 80% reserved capacity; validate noisy-neighbor eviction; validate per-route quota enforcement.
Quoted internal concerns: legal on data residency language, engineering on integration of KV prefix caching and SDK changes, finance on ARR commitment size.
Customer comment (VP Eng): "We can't have tail latency surprises — must have per-route SLA and control plane hooks for emergency throttles."
SE notes: propose 'priority lanes' feature map: token-weighted priority, per-route concurrency caps, adaptive backpressure, dry-run mode for routing changes.
